In its latest five-year plan, China has set its sights on developing five drugs that could each rake in more than $1 billion globally by 2030. Experts say it’s well on its way, with two medications having already met that bar.
Crucial to China’s goal of becoming a global biopharma juggernaut by 2030 is delivering at least five domestically developed blockbuster drugs with global sales topping $1 billion annually. Experts tell BioSpace that the Asian giant is already well on its way to hitting this target.
“Two have already crossed the [blockbuster] threshold,” Mark Lansdell, director at the life sciences intelligence firm Evaluate, told BioSpace in an email. And according to Evaluate data, at least four more are forecast to follow. The industry considers products that make $1 billion in annual sales to be blockbuster drugs.
Indeed, BeOne Medicines’ BTK blocker Brukinsa, first approved in late 2019 for mantle cell lymphoma, brought in $3.9 billion last year across what has become a broad range of indications. Meanwhile, Legend Biotech’s Johnson & Johnson partnered CAR T therapy Carvykti, indicated for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, hit $1.89 billion last year.
Next up is likely to be Guangdong-based Akeso’s ivonescimab, on which the company has partnered with Summit Therapeutics and is expecting an initial FDA approval as early as November . Evaluate expects the PD-1xVEGF to hit $4.4 billion in sales by 2030 across several indications, according to Lansdell.
Beyond Brukinsa, Carvykti and ivonescimab, Evaluate projects four other Chinese-developed medicines will bring in at least $1 billion yearly by 2030. Below, BioSpace takes a closer look at the products that could help the Asian giant hit the bold five-year goal and solidify its position as a global biopharma behemoth.

China plans to transform biotech sector into $522B powerhouse by 2030
A new five-year biotech plan has been released by the Chinese government, revealing ambitious goals such as achieving five blockbuster medicines on the global markets in that time.
September 18, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
BeOne’s Brukinsa, already a blockbuster, poised for expansion
Topping Evaluate’s list is BeOne’s BTK inhibitor Brukinsa , which is approved for a wide range of cancers, including mantle cell lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia.
Brukinsa already crossed the blockbuster bar, surging 49% year-on-year in 2025 to bring in $3.9 billion. The drug has continued to grow, with a 31% increase in Q2 sales to hit $1.2 billion. Evaluate forecasts the drug to reach $6.5 billion in annual global sales by 2030, according to data provided by Lansdell.
BeOne continues to study Brukinsa in other indications, including treatment-naive mantle cell lymphoma. Phase 3 data in June showed that Brukinsa plus the anti-CD20 antibody rituximab met the primary endpoint of progression-free survival in the Phase 3 MANGROVE study, reducing the risk of progression or death by 43% versus rituximab plus chemotherapy. A regulatory submission in this indication is slated for this year.
The company is also working to expand Brukinsa into marginal zone lymphoma and primary membranous nephropathy.
Legend Biotech’s J&J-partnered Carvykti faces potential competitive headwinds
Also already past the blockbuster line is the CAR T therapy Carvykti, originally developed by Legend Biotech, which was founded in 2015 as a subsidiary of the Nanjing-based contract developer GenScript.
In 2017, Legend scored a powerhouse partner in J&J, which fronted $350 million to work with the Chinese company to advance an anti-BCMA CAR T therapy that, in February 2022, would ultimately win the FDA’s go-ahead and hit the market as Carvykti. The multiple myeloma therapy made blockbuster status last year, bringing in $1.89 billion worldwide —nearly double its 2024 sales.
And Carvykti continues to climb, already surpassing full-year 2025 sales in the first nine months of this year with $1.96 billion, according to J&J’s most recent earnings report.
But there are some competitive headwinds on the horizon. By Dec. 23 , the FDA is scheduled to release a verdict for Gilead’s anitocabtagene autoleucel (anito-cel), another CAR T therapy that is being proposed for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. While the potential approval will be for fourth-line or later use, falling outside Carvykti’s established position in the second-line setting , Gilead plans to push anito-cel earlier, with a second-line filing ready as early as next year, the pharma said in its third quarter report .
Legend and J&J are continuing to test Carvykti as a frontline option for multiple myeloma.
Summit lines up ivonescimab as next major cancer backbone
Ivonescimab has emerged as one of the leading candidates for China’s blockbuster aspirations. The drug—originally developed by Guangdong-based Akeso and being tested globally in partnership with Summit Therapeutics—first captured the industry’s attention in September 2024 when it beat Merck’s mega-blockbuster therapy Keytruda in a head-to-head late-stage non-small cell lung cancer study.
And while there have been some hiccups, including an overall survival miss in a Phase 3 global study in May last year, analysts still expect that ivonescimab could be a commercial powerhouse. Other cancer drugmakers appear to agree, with AstraZeneca, Pfizer and more teaming up with Summit to pair their own assets into ivonescimab combos.
“If the data do pan out, then simply put, ivonescimab has the potential to replace Keytruda as the next major backbone of treatment in cancer—and in turn, to become the next best-selling oncology drug of all time,” Graig Suvannavejh, managing director and senior biotech and biopharma analyst at Mizuho Securities, told BioSpace .
Evaluate has estimated that ivonescimab could grow to an estimated $4.4 billion in global sales by 2030.

BeOne’s Tevimbra set for blockbuster status as early as 2027
BeOne’s second appearance on this list is for the PD-1 inhibitor Tevimbra, which according to Evaluate’s Lansdell is “forecast to pass $1 billion in annual sales as early as 2027.”
First approved by the FDA in March 2024 for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, Tevimbra has since expanded into gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. In the European Union, Tevimbra is also indicated for non-small cell lung cancer, small cell lung cancer and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
Across these indications, the drug last year jumped 19% from 2024 to earn $737 million globally. Tevimbra continues to trend upward, making $229 million in the second quarter, an 18% year-on-year increase—and a roughly 7% beat versus analyst expectations, according to an Aug. 6 note from Leerink Partners.
BeOne in August announced that the FDA approved the first-line use of Tevimbra, alongside Jazz Pharmaceuticals and Zymeworks’ anti-HER2 bispecific Ziihera, for advanced HER2+ gastric, gastroesophageal junction or esophageal adenocarcinoma. In a Jan. 6 note, Leerink said the Tevimbra-Ziihera combo was “clearly practice-changing” in this indication.
BeOne is also developing Tevimbra for urothelial bladder carcinoma and is working on a subcutaneous formulation for the drug. Both are in late-stage development.
Kelun-Biotech and Merck aim to replace chemo in NSCLC with Sac-TMT
Another Big Pharma–partnered asset on this list is sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) that was originally developed by Chengdu-based Kelun-Biotech. Merck in December 2022 paid $175 million upfront —and gambled up to $9.3 billion in milestones—for an exclusive global license to the asset and six other Kelun ADCs outside mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau.
Sac-TMT is currently being studied for several cancer types, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), bladder cancer, breast cancer and gastric cancer.
Early Phase 3 NSCLC data presented in July showed that sac-TMT plus Merck’s blockbuster drug Keytruda improved progression-free survival and showed a positive overall survival trend versus Keytruda plus chemotherapy. These findings suggest that sac-TMT could replace platinum-based chemotherapy as a first-line NSCLC treatment option.
Merck also presented data last month at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) meeting in Madrid showing that sac-TMT slashed the risk of death by 32% in a late-stage trial of endometrial cancer. Based on these results, the FDA accepted Merck’s application for approval of sac-TMT in this indication and granted priority review.
In December 2025, the FDA awarded sac-TMT a Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher , which can shorten review times from the typical 10–12 months to just 1–2 months. However, Leerink Partners analysts have noted that “it’s unclear to us whether the CNPV is still active after Commissioner Makary’s departure from FDA.” Still, the group said, Merck “is in discussions with the FDA and is hopeful for an earlier approval.”
Assuming U.S. approval and launch next year, Evaluate’s Lansdell projects sac-TMT to cross the blockbuster bar in 2029 and hit $2 billion in sales by 2030. The ADC is already approved in China for various types of breast cancer, but Kelun has yet to provide sales numbers.
Hansoh’s Ameile nears blockbuster status even without US approval
Another likely Chinese blockbuster is Hansoh Pharma’s Ameile, which first hit the global biopharma markets in 2020 after being approved in China for second-line treatment of patients with advanced NSCLC carrying the T790M EGFR mutation. The drug has since expanded into other NSCLC types and treatment settings in the Asian country.
Ameile is also approved outside China. In June 2025, the U.K.’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency greenlit the drug under the brand name Aumseqa, opening up use for certain NSCLC patients. The European Union in February likewise gave the go-ahead for Aumseqa, but walked back this decision in September after a legal challenge from AstraZeneca alleged that the regulatory submission for Hansoh’s drug violated data protection policies. Hansoh resubmitted the application last month.
There is no ongoing application for Ameile, also known as aumolertinib, in the U.S.
Despite the EU setback, Lansdell said Evaluate continues to project that Ameile will hit blockbuster status by 2030, though he didn’t provide a specific sales forecast for the drug.
In its annual 2025 and interim 2026 reports, Hansoh provided no sales figures for Amelie, but according to a September analysis by analytic and content platform VCBeat, Ameile made RMB 5.53 billion ($830 million) last year, making it the top-selling innovative drug in China.

2026 SEMA Show: Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
8 photos
Photo: Ford
There are so many cool things happening at the 2026 SEMA Show , like Billie the Pontiac GTO from Ringbrothers (just to give you an example off the top of our minds), that Ford felt compelled to break the norm. Then it sliced it into pieces, burned it, spread the ashes, and blew them away with a wind turbine rather than a simple leaf blower. Yeah, that pretty much sums it up.
Anyway, before we even consider talking about Frostwarden, let’s just say that the Blue Oval also had other interesting things to showcase. One of them was a 1966 Ford Mustang Fastback “built from heritage” and named Ford Racing R125. That’s because, quite obviously, it’s a Mustang Fastback with Ford Racing parts, making it a feisty restomod that celebrates Ford Racing’s 125th Anniversary with a 347-cubic-inch crate engine producing 360 horsepower and 400 lb.-ft. of torque and a Tremec TKX-600 five-speed transmission at its heart.
There are way more things going on with it, but we need to jump a couple of decades to reach Matt Johnson, a mechanical engineer who decided to morph a forgotten 1985 Ford F-250 into a “showstopper.” So, he took the $800 truck and made it look pretty, then dropped the ​​​​Ford Racing 460-cube small block in it with 575 hp and 575 lb-ft of torque. After becoming the water tank discussion subject in Dearborn, Ford reached out to him and convinced the builder to make it a SEMA contender.
Skip a few other decades, and we’re in present time right out in Las Vegas, Nevada, where the “SEMA builds do more than stop you in your tracks.” So, Ford aimed to be outrageous and over the top and make dreams possible, and the result is Frostwarden. The name is quite odd, since the only references outside of the Blue Oval news we could find are about a legendary melee weapon in Dungeon Quest or an ancient geomancer in Minecraft.
Anyway, the Blue Oval version is “the first vehicle to put the new Megazilla 2.0 crate engine swap on full display,” a Ford Bronco paired with a supercharged 7.3-liter V8 that can pack over 1,200 horsepower and over 1,000 lb.-ft. of torque. The SUV is strapped in with “the kind of hardware required to give that power an equally serious platform: 42-inch BFGoodrich tires, custom 18-inch Weld bead-lock wheels, 74Weld portal gear lifts, upgraded Dana driveline hardware, and custom Bilstein dampers.”
The brief was simple: “go big.” So, the Megazilla 2.0 is a “new development program with a stronger block, supercharger-specific camshaft, upgraded pistons, larger fuel injectors, a different belt drive and damper, and a 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple supercharger at the center of the package.” Ford says it’s the most powerful crate engine ever created by an automaker “based on race fuel per SAE J607 standard.”
The SUV is also leaning into the direction of a Bronco Arctic search-and-rescue rig, so the “42-inch tires, portal gear lifts, and wide stance give Frostwarden the presence of a serious winter recovery machine,” complete with all the attributes needed to stand out in a tall crowd as the one at the annual SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada. Of course, don’t count on this Bronco hitting the trails in series production form, quite sadly, as Ford expressly says it’s not quite up to snuff with the “federal safety standards.” It’s still cool, though.

Android Auto Cielo Update Could Include More Surprises, Android Auto 18.1 Code Shows
9 photos
Photo: Google
The Cielo update is undoubtedly a highly anticipated Android Auto update, and the closer we get to its launch, the more surprises are being discovered. This time, the newly released Android Auto 18.1 includes evidence that Google might be aiming for something that would make perfect sense: sync the debut of Cielo with the introduction of a new light theme.
It’s already feeling like Google has been working on the Android Auto light mode for ages, with evidence of these visual tweaks being in development spotted long ago.
But now it turns out that the search giant is making good progress on this front, and the new light theme is being developed side by side with the Cielo makeover. The objective might be a synced debut, so the introduction of Cielo, which will bring widgets and other new features, could also include a light mode.
A recent teardown of the Android Auto 18.1 APK includes mentions of the light mode being developed for Samsung phones, though there’s a very good chance that these tweaks are also planned for other Android devices, such as Google Pixel phones. Google wants the redesign to be available in both dark and light modes, so there’s no doubt that the same assets would eventually be available for all devices running Android Auto.
Google also seems to be making progress in the development of Cielo, with Android Auto 18.1 including mentions of the animations we’ll see when we interact with the redesigned interface.
The company has so far remained tight-lipped as to when we’re supposed to get our hands on Cielo, but considering all these new releases include more and more evidence that the update is coming, it’s probably safe to assume that the “coming soon” promise is actually happening this time.
The first beta users could get the new interface by the end of the year, and I expect the rollout to production devices to begin in the first quarter of 2027 before gaining more traction during the summer.
Photo: Google The Cielo update Google wants to completely transform the Android Auto experience in a way that makes more sense in new-generation cars.
This is why Android Auto will use the available screen estate more efficiently, no matter the shape, dimensions, or resolution. Right now, Android Auto is often centered and displayed in a rectangular panel on infotainment screens with unusual designs, and the introduction of Cielo will change that. The best example is the circular screen installed in MINI cars, where Android Auto will use the entire screen estate to run its apps, including Google Maps.
Google also wants the experience with Android Auto to feel smoother and more fluid. And because the purpose of Android Auto is to be an extension of Android, it’ll get new fonts and smoother animations, such as the ones that are currently being worked on and spotted in Android Auto 18.1.
Photo: Google Wallpapers will get new features and will be allowed to roam between devices when the user experience transitions from a phone to a car. The same wallpaper could appear on both screens, making the switch from one screen to the other smoother.
Google is also planning to unlock new app categories, and without a doubt, the topic that’s getting the most attention this time is the introduction of video apps. Google will finally enable YouTube videos on Android Auto , and the company even promises 60 fps full HD support in cars where such capabilities are possible.
The YouTube support will enable drivers to watch videos when their cars are stationary, while an audio-only mode will allow them to continue playback by listening to the audio track. Video playback will be locked when the car is in motion as a safety restriction. YouTube will require a Premium subscription for such capabilities, considering the ability to play videos in the background is not part of the free tier.
Photo: Google The last big update that’ll go live as part of the Cielo makeover is the integration of widgets. The long-term objective is to allow all Android applications that can show widgets on mobile devices to expand to Android Auto, but it’s unclear if this functionality will be available at launch.
Once widgets go live, the Android Auto UI will be divided into more floating panels appearing on the screen at the same time. Google Maps will be in the background and expand to the edges of the screen, while the rest of the apps, such as the media card on the Coolwalk screen, will be displayed as a floating panel.
Widgets will be displayed on the right of the screen, and users will be able to see the weather, the clock, their calendar entries, and pretty much anything that a widget shows without opening the full apps.
Considering the Cielo update is still in the works, many of these specifics might change before the rollout begins. However, Google’s original teasers certainly looked promising, and fingers crossed that it won’t take long before we get our hands on the same goodies.

BMW M 100 Jahre Nürburgring Edition That Marks 100 Years of Green Hell Also Comes to Australia
36 photos
Photo: BMW
The global BMW M “100 Jahre Nürburgring” Edition celebrates 100 years of legendary German track prowess, and fans in the Land Down Under get in on the action, though only partially.
Back in early September 2026, the premium German carmaker BMW announced a collection of nine cars and motorcycles tasked with one singular goal: celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Nürburgring track in Germany. The little town in Germany called Nurburg got its racetrack opened in 1927, and at the time probably nobody thought that the racing circuit, officially called the Nürburgring , would turn out to evolve into one of the most important pieces of asphalt and racing track elements in global automotive history.
Everyone comes here to test all the newest automobiles and technologies, at the same time competing against each other in a well-known yet undeclared war of hubris, trying to achieve the best lap times across the 13-mile (almost 21 km) version of the track known as the Nordschleife or the Green Hell. One German automaker, in particular, moved to obliterate the competition with its tribute to the track: BMW decided to celebrate the anniversary with no less than nine special vehicles with both two and four wheels.
More precisely, the fleet consists of six BMW M cars and three BMW Motorrad M motorcycles, all painted in Nürburgring Green and sporting Nordschleife motifs: M2, M3 sedan and Touring, M4 Coupe, plus the M5 sedan and Touring. The bikes, on the other hand, are the BMW M 1000 RR, M 1000 R, and M 1000 XR. How about Australia?
Well, the local division of BMW happily announced in early November 2026 that four models from the global roster have also been confirmed for the Land Down Under: BMW M2 xDrive, M3 Competition Sedan M xDrive, M4 Competition Coupe M xDrive, and the M5 Sedan. BMW M calls this gathering the exclusive “100 Jahre Nürburgring” edition, and only a very limited number of cars will make the trip to Australia in right-hand-drive form.
Yup, you need to hurry to snatch one of these special editions, as only 16 automobiles have been reserved for Australia . Pricing starts from AU$155,800 MRLP including GST and LCT, which is about $109k at the current exchange rate. BMW says Australia is a growing market for the M division, with almost 10% of the global sales of 2025 and 20% of the brand’s overall sales from January through September 2026.
All versions of the special edition wear the special BMW Individual Nürburgring Green paint finish on the outside, but there’s also an alternate mod in Black Sapphire metallic if anyone wants it. The most expensive option is the M5 Sedan, of course, which starts at no less than AU$280,800, which is the equivalent of more than $196k at the current exchange rate.

This 1956 Ford F-100 With 800 Horsepower Is the Truck Your Grandpa Wished He Had
7 photos
Photo: Fat Fender Garage
This is "the most ambitious truck we have ever built," said Fat Fender Garage when they unveiled the 1956 F-100 GT/FX at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas. The good, old truck comes with a Coyote V8 pumping out an incredible 800 horsepower at the crank and looking like the truck your grandpa wished he had when he young.
The 1956 Ford F-100 GT/FX is the brainchild of its owner, car collector Tony Peressini, who commissioned Fat Fender Garage (FFG) in Gilbert, Arizona, to bring his ultimate dream project to life. FFG CEO and founder Jason Noel was the one who supervised the project.
The mighty truck made its debut at the Meguiar’s booth at this year's SEMA as the result of 15,000 hours of work over five years, which involved hand-built fabrication, an engine swap, and a suspension rebuild. It "took every corner of the shop to pull this one off," say those involved in the build.
The restomodding experts brag about incorporating 70 years of Ford heritage in a single truck, which actually seems to cost as much as all those trucks, as Fat Fender Garage' s creation is estimated to cross the one million dollars mark.
Photo: Fat Fender Garage The truck was entirely reimagined from the floorboards up to deliver track-ready performance. The cab sits on an in-house-developed FF1 Performance coilover chassis, engineered from scratch by Fat Fender Garage, capable of providing sports car handling and high-speed stability.
Heavy-duty six-piston Wilwood front brakes up front and four-piston calipers out back, tucked neatly behind premium 20-inch HRE wheels with sticky Toyo Proxes Sport 2 tires, provide the stopping power. The sheet metal was heavily redesigned and hand-fabricated into a wider, flatter silhouette, riding mean and low. It sports a pancaked roof and hood for a flatter look.
The entire cab wasn't just chopped to lower the roofline, but it was sectioned by 2 inches. This procedure involved cutting a horizontal slice out of the middle of the cab's body panels and welding it back together, shrinking its vertical mass for a sleek profile. In the meantime, the front and rear track widths were increased via widened fenders and custom running boards.
Up front, a sharp chin splitter showed up, while a functional diffuser borrowed directly from a Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 and adapted to fit the truck was installed at the rear. The diffuser is designed to manage high-speed airflow underneath the truck bed.
Photo: Fat Fender Garage The grille on Tony Peressini's 1956 Ford F-100 GT/FX is a deliberate preservation of classic Ford styling on the entire million-dollar build. While Fat Fender Garage spent over 15,000 hours aggressively chopping, sectioning, widening, and reshaping every other single square inch of the truck's steel body, the original front grille was left completely stock.
However, the bumper and exterior trim pieces have been treated with a sleek Cerakote finish instead of the traditional chrome. Cerakote is a specialized ceramic-based thin-film coating originally designed for firearms and military hardware to withstand extreme heat, abrasion, and corrosion, so it’s obvious that the F-100 build is made to last.
The truck features flush-mounted glass all around to eliminate old rubber seals, carbon-fiber side mirrors, and a completely unique, handcrafted cargo bed. The GT/FX truck is painted in ultra-premium, custom champagne BASF paint, complete with an in-house hand-finished racing stripe.
The interior of the 70-year-old F-100 brings high-end sports car vibes, as the layout of the bare-bones utility truck from the 1950s has been entirely overhauled. Custom black leather covers the sports bucket seats and the dash pad. The original analog instrument cluster has been replaced by a set of modern custom gauges, calibrated directly to read data from the supercharged Gen-3 Coyote and provide the relevant driving data.
Photo: Fat Fender Garage A premium infotainment touchscreen was seamlessly integrated into the dashboard. To preserve the ultra-clean lines across the dashboard, Fat Fender Garage engineered a completely hidden climate control system that blows air through a single concealed horizontal vent. Fat Fender Garage also came up with a modern sound system.
However, the 1956 F-100 GT/FX is not all show and no go. Lurking beneath that custom steel hood is a third-generation Ford 5.0-liter Coyote V8, topped with a massive 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger. The setup pushes out an incredible 800 horsepower and 750 pound-feet of torque.
A Ford 10R80 ten-speed automatic transmission, operated via a newly fabricated, floor-mounted sport shifter installed in the center console, puts the power down through the rear wheels. A bespoke 3-inch system equipped with Borla XR-1 Raceline mufflers, JDM resonators, and electronic cutouts roars out all the drama of the supercharged V8.
The 1956 Ford F-100 GT/FX that you are looking at is not for sale. It is a privately owned, one-off commission built specifically for corporate executive and car collector Tony Peressini, who funded the five-year, million-dollar passion project to create his personal dream truck. It will go straight to his garage once SEMA wraps up in Las Vegas. He surely won't be able to fly under the radar in it.

News
AMD Q3 2026 Earnings Summary
AMD posted a massive Q3 2026. Revenue hit $13.377 billion, up 45% year over year and 16% sequentially. Data Center revenue reached $8.546 billion, up 97% year over year. Embedded Revenue was up big, and client revenue fared better than Intel in many respects.
AMD Has Record Quarter Driven By Data Center
Here is AMD’s Q3 2026 summary slide. This is an enormous quarter. Embedded revenue was up 29% year over year, and yet that almost feels like a footnote.
AMD Q3 2026 Earnings Summary
AMD delivered GAAP operating income of $2.832 billion on revenue of $13.377 billion, with net income of $2.428 billion and diluted earnings per share of $1.46. On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes stock-based compensation, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and other items, operating income was $3.923 billion, net income was $3.471 billion and EPS came in at $2.09.
AMD Q3 2026 GAAP Financial Results
Even the quarterly numbers were up a lot, with 16% growth on the GAAP side.
AMD’s Data Center Is Big Time
The Data Center segment generated $8.546 billion in revenue, up 97% year over year and 27% sequentially. AMD attributes this Data Center surge to strong EPYC demand and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs. The company says major clients, including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, are running workloads on Helios rack-scale solutions powered by these chips.
AMD Q3 2026 Data Center Results
The comparison to Intel’s data center results from last week saw its quarterly revenue of $7.3 billion, up 78% year-over-year. AMD’s Data Center segment at $8.546 billion grew faster at 97%. Both companies are clearly seeing surging demand for AI infrastructure and server processors, but AMD seems to be accelerating.
Venice is coming, and we expect AMD to have clear x86 performance leadership, as Intel’s PCIe Gen6 Diamond Rapids platform , we expect, will be later in 2027. On technical merits, we expect AMD to be in a great place, and it seems like AMD is better managing its supply to get chips out.
AMD Client and Gaming Segment
The combined Client and Gaming segment saw revenue down 8% year-over-year, at $3.722 billion. Client notched up a bit, while gaming went down. Memory and NAND prices are keeping a lid on this market.
AMD Q3 2026 Client And Gaming Results
Of note, AMD said its Ryzen AI Halo Platform with the Ryzen AI Max Pro 400 series is not available, so that means Gorgon Halo? We will have our first Gorgon Halo review soon, as that machine is running benchmarks now. Somewhat notable on the slide is that AMD has three AI-related products highlighted, while Intel’s three summary bullets on its CCPG segment were focused on shortages, demand for future products, and a generic AI PC nod. AMD, with the Strix Halo platform, at least has something it can use to run reasonably large models locally, and you have to wonder if that is a driver here.
AMD’s Embedded Grows
The Embedded segment delivered $1.109 billion in revenue, up 29% year-over-year. AMD says growth came from aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets.
AMD Q3 2026 Embedded Results
Just as a frame of reference, Xilinx’s annual revenue was something like $3.1-3.2B when AMD completed its acquisition of Xilinx . In most markets, if you grow 29% year over year and see a huge margin increase, it is time to throw a party. This seems to simply offset client’s (gaming) weakness.
AMD Q4 Guidance Points To Acceleration
AMD expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of approximately $17 billion plus or minus 3%. At the midpoint, that represents year-over-year growth of about 66% and sequential growth of roughly 27%.
AMD Q4 2026 Financial Outlook
If this quarter seems big, then next quarter seems like it will be significantly bigger.
Final Words
AMD has its Helios rack-scale infrastructure rolling out, and Venice. Ryan recently went into the Venice architecture . If AMD was ahead in many metrics with its Turin generation , then adding more cores, updated cores, and higher memory bandwidth should be a recipe for clear x86 socket leadership, at least until Intel is able to field Diamond Rapids. It will be interesting to see how much of a price premium AMD can extract for a generational advantage and first-mover status. Socket refresh generations are less exciting than the Turin-to-Venice transition, which is a major platform update (DDR5 channel count and PCIe Gen6). That also means PCIe Gen6 development, like PCIe Gen4, will likely happen more often on AMD than on Intel. Gluing chips together seems to be working out reasonably well.

BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree Louisa Helms is a lot of things—athlete, scientist, entrepreneur and likely future biotech executive. Just don’t ask her to pick up any pipettes.
Louisa Helms had a real-life Ms. Frizzle as her librarian in high school. Instead of a magic school bus, however, her Ms. Frizzle had a flow cytometer and 3D printer, and she’d take students on field trips to real labs.
This is how Helms, now a partner at Flagship Pioneering, got into biotech. The librarian’s name was Tammy Carabello, and she provided a model of lifetime learning for Helms and her peers at that Seattle high school. Carabello later became a biotech teacher and ultimately went back to school for her PhD.
Flagship’s Louisa Helms.
KenRichardsonphoto2025
“She’s my guiding light,” Helms, who was recently named one of BioSpace ’s 40 Under 40 leaders, said in an interview. “And she introduced me to Cat in the Hat when I was even younger. So, like, best of both worlds.”
Now, Helms is lighting her own way. After her high school experience, she pursued science, taking a break before her PhD to consider what she would do with her education. “I wanted to be making decisions in science, and the people who make decisions in science are in positions of power,” she said.
After completing her education, Helms began entrepreneurial training to prepare for a career as a decision-maker. She found herself working with venture capitalists and companies in the Seattle ecosystem. In 2022, she got a major break. She applied for a job at renowned biotech venture firm Flagship.
“Flagship was notorious. I knew what it was, and the role was just this, like mystical, mysterious, mythical, perfect role,” Helms said.

BioSpace 40 Under 40 winners make their mark on biopharma
40 Under 40 honorees’ accomplishments include co-developing the world’s first synthetic biology programming language for mRNA and co-founding and leading a company acquired for $700 million up-front and up to $1.225 billion in total consideration.
October 6, 2026

To Helms’ surprise, she got the job.
“It’s become everything I thought it would be, and more,” Helms said of the job, which she began in 2022. “It was an entrepreneurial training ground, such that we would actually learn what warrants taking a scientific idea and turning it commercial and turning it into something you would build and test.”
The first company Helms got to help build was Serif Biomedicines, which officially launched in April with a mission to develop modified DNA medicines. She remembers helping design experiments, ordering reagents and working with the scientists who were executing the vision. She also jumped in to help with corporate development and helped build out a therapeutics workstream for a program.
“My involvement in the company has been extremely all-encompassing but what I’m really proud of is just the impact on the science I was able to make early,” Helms said.
She clarifies—with a laugh—that she wasn’t actually at the bench. “I do not touch pipettes. That would be a disservice to these companies.”
Rather, she offers up her unique range of skills whenever she is needed on the job. Beyond biotech, Helms is an athlete, competing in CrossFit where her “training mindset” comes from. This is a point of pride, she says, that has kept her grounded and taught her discipline and the value of hard work. “I think people forget that by being a whole human, you do your job better than when you’re just a work human,” she said.

Securing financing that allowed an exit from academia, leaving ecology and evolutionary biology for biomedical engineering and shifting from business development to entrepreneurship are among key turning points for three biopharma professionals.

Helms has now risen to principal at Flagship and is credited as a co-founder of Serif. The biotech has since launched out of the Flagship universe and Helms is mostly on to her next project, a secretive biotech that remains undercover. Her exact role in the next venture is yet to be determined and she demurred at the suggestion that she might serve as CEO. She’s learning at Flagship how to step back for the right people.
That said, Helms emphasized that her ultimate goal is to be a serial biotech CEO—a role many of her Flagship peers also embrace.
“I’m lucky that I get to kind of stay connected to Serif and see it mature and grow,” she said, “but what is important about our role at Flagship is knowing when to hire yourself out of your job and give it to someone who’s doing it better than you.”
